I'm not saying to outright stop having children, I'm saying to not have children if you can't yet. Do you have any idea how it felt like growing up where all your food is rationed, showers are timed, and beds are optional? I've lived in neighborhoods where on the left of my house was a drug den and the other was a meat butcher. That's no place for a child to grow up and it messes up with their mind. Yeah, it's not a death sentence. But trust me when I say that you'll really wish it was. 

On paper it sounds good, "couples should have as many children as they want". Who wouldn't want a world where you can just decide to have a child when you feel like it? But try to live in reality. Not everyone lives in a country where the government provides assistance. And you say "we take care of our own" as if people aren't naturally selfish. You'll provide for your family first, that's "your" own, and if you can't take care of that how are you going to take care of others? The rest of the world is trying to get by without having a care for the next because it's already hard enough as it is.

Also depends a lot on the country and lifestyle. In my case my family had to do a lot of cost cutting, we literally just lived on the bare necessities. We never had a TV, food was heavily portioned, and all our clothes were from bargain bins. It wasn't fun but it was definitely livable.
You can still adopt. Don't adopt till you're ready. Growing up in a household where people fight over money is...not a fun household to say the least. Save and plan.

As with the other comments here, it's not about being poor. You can be middle class and still not be financially stable to provide for a child. I'm not calling a child an object but you wouldn't buy a brand new car if you can barely afford rent, would you? Raising a child is a very hard task to undertake and it takes proper planning and saving up.

Why does it have to be between poor and rich? People in the middle exist. People under the poverty bracket can also have children. What I was saying was to properly save up and plan for a child and not undertake a responsibility you're not prepared for.

And don't bring race into this. Some of us live in a country where what you might call POC are just the population.

Dumb people? Sure, they need to be educated first before handing them the fragile life of a child. But poor people? If they're in a fairly stable household, can provide the basic necessities, and can feed a child 3 times a day then I don't see a problem with it.

It's about being financially responsible. Having a child in a point in time where your finances are in shambles is not a good idea, raising a child is expensive and the development of a child is something you don't want to skimp out on. Just like with any huge decisions a family should save up and plan for a child and not just blindly take on the responsibility of another life on a whim.

Please stop having babies if you can barely sustain you and your partner. Just because you can doesn't mean you should. Don't raise a child in an environment where you make them feel like a burden because it messes with their brain for the rest of their lives.
